proposal.original_claim_summary: Trump Threatens Universities with Tax-Exempt Status Revocation Over DEI
proposal.original_synopsis: Trump issued threats in February 2025 to revoke the tax-exempt status of universities that did not comply with his executive orders banning diversity, equity, and inclusion programs in educational institutions. The threats were directed at Harvard, Columbia, and other elite universities that resisted the orders. Legal experts argued the IRS cannot revoke tax-exempt status as political retaliation, and doing so would violate the First Amendment. University presidents warned that the coercive threats amounted to government censorship of academic content. The action was widely condemned as an unprecedented federal intrusion into the governance of private educational institutions.

frozen_original.title: DOGE Fires 1,500 NIH Scientists and Researchers
frozen_original.synopsis: In March 2025, the Department of Government Efficiency directed the firing of approximately 1,500 NIH scientists, researchers, and support staff — roughly one-sixth of the agency's total workforce — through a combination of mass terminations and buyout programs that stripped the NIH of experienced researchers in cancer, Alzheimer's, HIV, rare diseases, and emerging infectious diseases. Many of those fired were mid-career scientists with unique expertise and active research programs with no clear successors. Ongoing clinical trials enrolling thousands of patients faced disruption or cancellation. NIH grant peer review panels lost quorum as members resigned in protest. Academic medical centers that relied on NIH training grants reported being unable to maintain research programs. Former NIH directors called the firings an act of scientific self-sabotage that would set U.S. biomedical research back a generation.

frozen_original.title: DOGE accesses VA medical records without patient consent
frozen_original.synopsis: DOGE operatives accessed Veterans Affairs medical records without patient consent, exposing sensitive health information of millions of veterans in violation of federal privacy law. The unauthorized access to VA medical systems included records containing combat-related injuries, PTSD diagnoses, and other sensitive mental health information for millions of veterans. Veterans service organizations filed lawsuits demanding the data be secured, warning that the breach could expose veterans to discrimination and harm.
